summary: Unexpected route drift to EU edge observed during US-WEST maintenance causing p95 latency spikes for ByteHealth
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (ByteHealth, enterprise) reports a sudden increase in p95 generation latency beginning at 2026-03-12 15:02 UTC. Traffic which should be served from us-west is observed to route to eu-west-1 for a subset of requests, causing additional network hop and TLS handshake time.

Impact:
- Higher p95 latency (~2200ms -> ~4200ms) for production inference calls for one of customer’s pinned routes.
- Errors not reported, but user-visible slowness affecting time-sensitive workflows.

Environment:
- Production, us-west region (primary).
- Dedicated enterprise tenancy for ByteHealth with strict_residency enabled.

Steps to reproduce observed by customer:
1) Send repeated generation calls to customer’s pinned endpoint from us-west clients.
2) Observe occasional responses with additional 1800-2200ms latency and remote endpoint resolving to eu-west-1 IP.
3) Reproduces intermittently (~5-12% of requests) and clustered around control-plane maintenance window (2026-03-12 14:55–15:15 UTC).

Observed logs / artifacts:
- Edge proxy logs (route-decision.log) show control_plane:bind_expiry refresh events at 2026-03-12T14:58:23Z and 15:04:10Z.
- Route decisions include fallback path entry "residency_fallthrough: true" for ~7% of requests from this customer.
- tcpdump captures show TLS handshake to eu-west IPs adding ~1.9s to duration.
- Customer-provided request IDs: [req-7f12a, req-7f13d, req-7f1be] (attached in ticket).

Temporary workaround requested by customer:
- Advice to pause non-critical maintenance or to toggle route strictness if possible.
- We provided a temporary mitigation: forced refresh of residency-binding for the tenant via control-plane API (see investigation notes).
comments: 2026-03-12 15:20 - Ava Martinez (Support): Received customer report. Confirmed latency spike and cross-region endpoints in logs. Escalating to SRE. Added customer to P1 queue and set SLA due at 17:30Z.

2026-03-12 15:35 - Nikhil Rao (SRE): Beginning investigation. Noting maintenance activity in control-plane for key distribution during window 14:55-15:15Z. Hypothesis: partial binding refresh caused stale sticky-route entries to fall through to nearest available region (eu-west-1).

2026-03-12 16:05 - Priya Singh (Networking): Observed DNS re-resolve behavior from some edge proxies; TTLs are 30s but control-plane signalled a large routing topology change which triggered a conservative fallthrough path for some sticky sessions. We see ~6% of flows pick the fallback path.

2026-03-12 16:40 - ByteHealth (Customer rep - Jonah Park): We're seeing intermittent user timeouts on scheduled tasks — a stopgap of any kind would help. Asked if we can pin the customer explicitly to a us-west edge until the control-plane change finishes.

2026-03-12 16:55 - Nikhil Rao (SRE): Performed forced binding refresh for ByteHealth tenant (control-plane call: POST /v1/admin/tenants/bytehealth/refresh-binding). Early telemetry shows p95 dropping back to baseline on recent checks but still watching for recurrence.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 15:40 - Collected edge-proxy and route-decision logs. Noted 'residency_fallthrough' flags correlate to maintenance timeline.
2026-03-12 15:52 - Verified no GPU capacity exhaustion on us-west serving pool; serving-runtime healthy. Counts show sufficient capacity.
2026-03-12 16:10 - Checked control-plane deployment: rolling config push to routing agents completed at 14:57Z but some agents reported delayed ACKs until 15:03Z (see infra/deploy logs).

2026-03-12 16:20 - Hypothesis: rolling update produced a short window where route-binding TTLs expired while control-plane agents had inconsistent topology view, causing a fallback selection to EU for a subset of requests.
2026-03-12 16:30 - Reproduced locally by simulating agent ACK delay and observed similar ~5–10% fallthrough in route-decisions.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied: issued tenant-level binding refresh which cleared stale sticky-route entries and returned affected requests to us-west; recommended customer temporarily pause non-essential traffic during control-plane maintenance windows. Root cause: short window of topology inconsistency during rolling control-plane update combined with default fallthrough policy and TTL timing.

Permanent fix plan (next steps):
- Engineering to implement a safety gating on topology rollouts that prevents fallthrough selection during overlap windows (ticket INT-4421).
- Reduce binding/route TTL jitter and add a grace period for sticky-route retention across rollouts.
- Improve observability: add a metric for 'fraction of requests using fallthrough path' and an alert threshold for >1% for enterprise tenants.

Status: patch scheduled for 2026-03-18; monitoring dashboard added to SRE runbook. Customer notified of mitigation and ETA for permanent fix.
